a: Cache-Control headers tell browsers and proxies how to cache responses.
ETags help clients revalidate cached resources efficiently.
Cookies store small data the browser sends back on later requests.
Sessions associate multiple requests with one logged-in user.
Browsers send OPTIONS preflight for some cross-origin requests.
Gzip compression reduces response size over the network.
WebSockets provide full-duplex communication over a long-lived connection.
HTTP/2 multiplexes streams over one connection for efficiency.
Clients can send idempotency keys so retries do not double-charge.
Content-Type declares the media type of the body.
